purpose: Citation record for NSM_RESOLUTIONS.md. Full texts are not committed; each quotation was checked against the full text named here, and quotations from scanned pages also against the page image.
page_convention: Manuscript pages for G12, G15 and GY14; printed pages otherwise.
copies: data/external/references/ (git-ignored). CATALOG.json there records each file's sha256, size, pagination offset, text method and provenance.

W1999.citation: Wierzbicka, Anna. 1999. Emotions across Languages and Cultures: Diversity and Universals. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (Studies in Emotion and Social Interaction, Second Series). ISBN 0 521 59042 6 (hb), 0 521 59971 7 (pb).
W1999.read: chapter 2 (pp.49-122) whole; chapter 1 section 9 (pp.38-45). The text layer is an OCR of a page scan; every quoted line was checked against the page image.
pages_quoted: p.50 (the nouns do not always mean the same as the corresponding adjectives)
p.56 (pleasure: no cognitive scenario; only the feeling is good)
pp.62-63 (sad: no thought-to-feeling link, and why)
p.97 (shocked; section 5: evaluations not aligned with the feeling)

W1990b.citation: Wierzbicka, Anna. 1990. The semantics of emotions: Fear and its relatives in English. Australian Journal of Linguistics 10(2): 359-375. (The journal's running head misprints the year as 1988.)
W1990b.read: whole. Every explication and every quoted passage was checked against the page images.
pages_quoted: pp.359-360 (sad, joy, anger; the hatred aside)
p.361 (BECAUSE vs AS; the 'I don't know why' test)
pp.363-373 (the fear family: fear, afraid, scared, fright, frightened, terrified, petrified, horrified, dread, alarmed, panic, anguish, anxiety, worried, concerned, apprehension)
p.366 (frighten occurs only in a dictionary comment)

GW2014.citation: Goddard, Cliff and Anna Wierzbicka. 2014. Words and Meanings: Lexical Semantics across Domains, Languages, and Cultures. Oxford: Oxford University Press. ISBN 978-0-19-966843-4.
pages_quoted: p.56 (categorization by KIND, qualification by LIKE)
p.59 (salty soup is not a category)
p.120 ([H] happiness as an emotion: no BECAUSE)

W1992-SCC.citation: Wierzbicka, Anna. 1992. Semantics, Culture, and Cognition: Universal Human Concepts in Culture-Specific Configurations. New York: Oxford University Press. ISBN 0-19-507325-8.
W1992-SCC.copy_of_record: data/external/references/wierzbicka-1992-semantics-culture-and-cognition.pdf (git-ignored; supplied by Rohan, F141; image-only scan, OCR made here)
W1992-SCC.read: contents, and the opening of chapter 4 (pp.135-136), which introduces a survey of emotion concepts of other languages. The rest was not read; nothing in the packet rests on it.

CH.citation: Chart of NSM Semantic Primes [v20, 10 May 2022]. nsm-approach.net.
CH.read: whole (pdftotext -layout of the copy of record; boxes also checked visually)

G12.citation: Goddard, Cliff. 2012. Semantic primes, semantic molecules, semantic templates: Key concepts in the NSM approach to lexical typology. Linguistics 50(3): 711-743. Author manuscript, Griffith Research Online hdl 10072/46996.
pages_quoted: p.3 (Table 1: no CAUSE; THIS, THE SAME, OTHER~ELSE are determiners; KIND, PART relational substantives)

G15.citation: Goddard, Cliff. 2015. The complex, language-specific semantics of 'surprise'. Review of Cognitive Linguistics 13(2). Accepted manuscript, Griffith Research Online hdl 10072/166643.
pages_quoted: p.14 (its frighten, attributed to W1990b, is not in W1990b)

GY14.citation: Goddard, Cliff and Zhengdao Ye. 2014. Exploring 'happiness' and 'pain' across languages and cultures. International Journal of Language and Culture 1(2). Author manuscript, Griffith Research Online hdl 10072/65273.

GW07.citation: Goddard, Cliff and Anna Wierzbicka. 2007. NSM analyses of the semantics of physical qualities: sweet, hot, hard, heavy, rough, sharp in cross-linguistic perspective. Studies in Language 31(4): 765-800.
GW07.note: GW2014 chapter 3 restates these passages and supersedes them by date; the packet now quotes GW2014.

TVS19.citation: Tissari, Heli, Ulla Vanhatalo and Mari Siiroinen. 2019. From corpus-assisted to corpus-driven NSM explications: The case of Finnish viha (anger, hate). Lege Artis IV(1): 290-334.
TVS19.read: sections 1-5 (appendices not read, not relied on)
TVS19.note: Its first-round definitions of vihata were written by Ulla Vanhatalo and Cliff Goddard. Page numbers were lost in extraction; cited by section.

FBG22.citation: Fenyvesi, Katalin, Eckhard Bick and Klaus Geyer. 2022. Sadness-related expressions in Danish and German: A corpus-assisted NSM-analysis. Scandinavian Studies in Language 13(1): 249-273. doi:10.7146/sss.v13i1.135080. CC BY 4.0.
FBG22.secondary_quotations: Wierzbicka 1999 'sad' (p.265), now confirmed against W1999 p.62 in every prime; Goddard 2018's template as applied to Danish and German (pp.265-266)

K.citation: Kitis, Eliza. Emotions as discursive constructs: The case of the psych-verb 'fear'. Author-hosted PDF.
K.secondary_quotations: Wierzbicka 1999: 75, 'fear' and 'afraid', now confirmed against W1999 p.75 in every prime. Kitis is a critic of NSM; the paper is no longer needed for any quotation.

W1992.citation: Wierzbicka, Anna. 1992. Defining emotion concepts. Cognitive Science 16(4): 539-581. doi:10.1207/s15516709cog1604_4.
W1992.access: Marked 'Free Access' by Wiley; text fetched from https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1207/s15516709cog1604_4 (43 pages)
W1992.read: whole, as extracted text; most explication blocks were lost in extraction, so only surviving lines are quoted
sections_quoted: The need for prototypes and scripts (BECAUSE vs LIKE; relief, disappointment, surprise, amazement)
Defining emotion concepts ('feel' vs 'be' frames; 'X was afraid' thought)
classification themes (love, hate, pity, envy set aside)
